description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of core software engineering principles, including requirements engineering using UML 2.5 for modeling; software design with object-oriented methodologies such as Java Design Patterns and the Gang of Four patterns; version control with Git and GitHub workflows; testing strategies including unit testing with JUnit 5 and integration testing with TestNG; software quality assurance through ISO/IEC 25010 standards; and project management using Agile Scrum with Jira. Students will also study architectural design patterns like MVC and microservices, and explore software lifecycle models such as Waterfall, Spiral, and V-model. Topics include software maintenance, refactoring techniques, and the application of design patterns to real-world systems. The course emphasizes the practical application of these concepts through hands-on projects and case studies.

clos.text: Define the key principles of software engineering and explain how they apply to real-world system development using UML 2.5 and Agile Scrum methodologies.
Describe the software development lifecycle models, including Waterfall, Spiral, and V-model, and evaluate their suitability for different project contexts.
Explain the role of software design patterns such as Factory, Singleton, and Observer in solving common software architecture problems.
Apply unit testing and integration testing techniques using JUnit 5 and TestNG to ensure software quality and reliability.
Implement a software project from requirements gathering to deployment using Git version control, Agile Scrum, and ISO/IEC 2,5010 quality assurance standards.

topics: Software Design Principles and Object-Oriented Design
Software Design Patterns: Gang of Four Patterns
Version Control with Git and GitHub
Agile Scrum and Project Management with Jira
Architectural Design Patterns: MVC and Microservices
Final Project Planning and Requirements Analysis
